reason:
The formula itself reproduces (see reproduced_numbers) and, as a population n→∞ object, is a correct closed form. What does not follow is the stated experimental consequence: that it "gives §7.11 a closed-form width criterion at any m" and that at (200,128) the q90≤0.15 tolerance "can be met for coefficient-bounded g (0.119)" so that "the response class is a user decision that changes the 128 verdict". Checked against the decision the obstacle actually poses (32→128 for the degree-2 corrected score at n=200, over the compatible set, with question clustering and an unknown F):

1. The criterion is for w_1, not for the quantity the decision needs. At the design itself (n=200, m=128, degree 2, production function) the realised width is systematically above w_1: narrow q50/q90 = 1.06×/1.34–1.43× w_1 (HC1 and CR1), half-variance world (which the round's own check1b places in the compatible set) non-PD 12.6%, q50 = 0.184 vs w_1 0.143, q90 = ∞; wide 1.09×. The inflation is not a constant factor, so no fixed correction turns w_1 into a q90 bound. The claim's own does-not-claim concedes this for m=32 but the consequence then silently uses w_1≤0.15 as the q90 criterion at m=128.

2. The positive half of the consequence fails under the author's own model. The c2 "sup" 0.119 combines the η-term maximum (attained at g≡0) with the g-term maximum (attained at |β|=2), which are not attained together; the library's c2 maximiser (−1,2,0) actually has w_1=0.096 and q90=0.134. But the c2-class member g = 2r−0.4 (|β_1|=2, osc=2, no clipping) has w_1=0.1186 ≈ the sup and realised q90 = 0.166–0.168 at (200,128) narrow, P(width>0.15)=18%. So "can be met for coefficient-bounded g" is false at the design; the tolerance is not met for either class in the narrow world, and the "user decision on the response class" does not change the 128 verdict.

3. Preconditions the real pipeline does not supply:
 (a) q_±=r±g/2 symmetric arms (hence σ²≤r(1−r)/8) is nowhere in the plan; the plan supports only σ²≤1/32. Under that bound the first-order c2 sup is 0.1385 (still <0.15) but realised q90 at (200,128) narrow is 0.170–0.177 even for the linear g (P>0.15 = 20–27%).
 (b) "No question effect in r or Δ beyond r; HC1 and CR1 estimate the same B" — the obstacle explicitly lists the within-question correlation model as an input, and §7.11 mandates CR1 by question because it is expected. With an additive question effect in Δ (sd 5–10 pp) the CR1 first-order B differs from the formula with a layout-dependent sign: shared-question layout (both types from the same frontier question, K_pref=4) makes w_1 conservative (×0.86–0.97), disjoint-question layout makes it anti-conservative (×1.10–1.34 first order; realised CR1 q90 0.165–0.204 at (200,128)). The plan does not fix how the 100+100 h_3 are spread over questions, so the formula is neither an upper nor a lower bound under real conditions.
 (c) Per-arm size: the plan gives 32 continuations per arm split 16/16 fit/eval and never says the endpoint contrast Δ̂_i uses 16 per arm. With 32 per arm the realised q90 for g=2r−0.4 drops from 0.166 to 0.136 (and w_1 0.1186→0.093) — the same unstated choice flips the verdict the other way. So the 128 verdict hinges on an analysis-plan detail, not on the response class.
 (d) F unknown: the closed form needs per-type moments ≤8 and D; the route's own claim 2 (§2.6) says the plug-in from the 32-pilot is unusable in the narrow regime (λ_min(Ĥ_w)≤0 in 69% of pilots, D̂ sd 0.12 vs D 0.18). So the real pipeline cannot evaluate the criterion with the precision the decision needs; the claim's worlds are the author's Beta choices, while the obstacle asks for the compatible set.
 (e) The "first-order m-budget" (narrow 32/64/192) is unusable below m≈128, not only at 32: at m=64 the production function is non-PD 20% with q50 0.168–0.179 and q90=∞, so the "64 for c2" entry is a second false positive of the same kind the claim flags for 32.
 (f) Minor: common m and Bin(m,r) hold if the executor follows §7.2b/§7.11 (selection on y₂ text/judge label, not on the 32 counts; judge error only redefines r), so these preconditions are satisfiable; n_t=100 matches.

Net: nothing in the Phase-0 design changes. The 32-vs-128 decision still rests on the finite-sample non-PD rate and realised width over the compatible set (check1/check1b, Route B/C), which the first-order width does not bound; the only surviving use of A-C1 is as the m→∞ sanity limit and as a lower-side plausibility check (a first-order width already >0.15 is sufficient for a negative verdict, as in the full-class narrow case).
fix: Restate the consequence as: "w_1 is the n→∞ width of the degree-2 corrected score under independent prefixes and symmetric 16-draw arms; at (n,m)=(200,128) the realised width is 1.06×(median) to 1.3–1.6×(q90) w_1 in the narrow world and unbounded (12.6% non-PD) in the half-variance world, so w_1≤0.15 is necessary but not sufficient for q90≤0.15; a first-order width >0.15 is a valid negative verdict, a first-order width <0.15 is not a positive one." Drop "can be met for coefficient-bounded g" and "the response class changes the 128 verdict" (counterexample g=2r−0.4: q90 0.166–0.168). Drop the m-budget line or restrict it to m≥128 (m=64: 20% non-PD). Add to scope: no question effect in Δ (else B_CR1 ≠ B_HC1 with layout-dependent sign; give the shared/disjoint formulas B_CR1 = B + τ²·{−e², +3e²} per prefix with e=D/w_1), the arm model (only σ²≤1/32 is plan-supported; report the sup under it), and the per-arm sample size (16 vs 32) as an explicit input. Mark the Beta worlds as illustrations, not the compatible set, and state that the pilot plug-in of the formula is unreliable in the narrow regime per the route's own claim 2. If the authors want a decision-relevant certificate, it must be stated for the realised q90/non-PD at n=200 (Route C's sequential design or a bootstrap-calibrated inflation of w_1), not for w_1.
strongest_attack_tried: Ran the production estimator endpoint_contrast_poly_cs at the real design (n=200, m=128, degree 2, HC1 and CR1, 2000 reps) on members of the author's own coefficient-bounded class under the author's own symmetric-arm model: g = 2r−0.4 (|β_1|=2, osc=2, no clipping) has w_1=0.1186 ≈ the claimed sup 0.119 but realised q90 = 0.166 (HC1) / 0.168 (CR1), P(width>0.15)=18%, so the "can be met for coefficient-bounded g" verdict fails at the design. Then removed one unstated precondition at a time: the plan-supported σ²≤1/32 arm model pushes even the linear g to q90 0.172–0.177; a 5–10 pp question effect in Δ under a disjoint-question layout pushes CR1 q90 to 0.165–0.204; the author's m=64 budget point is 20% non-PD; the half-variance (200,128) world is 12.6% non-PD with q50 0.184. Conversely 32 draws per arm (also consistent with the plan text) brings q90 to 0.136 — showing the 128 verdict is driven by analysis-plan details the claim does not pin down, not by the response class. Also attempted the sup over {|g|≤1 on the risk support only} (narrow sup 0.35, half-var 0.76): the "uniform" verdict is entirely a property of the author-chosen [0,1] class.
